rationale: validation_status=fail and analyzer_status=fail despite mutation_score=1.0 and coverage_score=1.0. The failures stem from SR5 being a dead check (it is a static self-test of the evaluator's own fixture rather than a check on the participant's submission content, so it never emits FAIL regardless of what is submitted) and FR3/FR4 being untested by the mutation harness (0 mutants target these requirements, leaving their correctness unverified).
revision_instructions: Two fixes required in evaluate.py: (1) SR5 currently never emits [TEST] FAIL on any mutant because it tests a fixed internal fixture rather than grading the actual submitted report content. Rewrite SR5 so it actively grades the submission at submission/trojan_report.json: it must FAIL if the submission is functionally equivalent to the naive baseline (infected=false, empty suspect_nodes, empty primary_output_affected) unless that submission also independently satisfies SR1-SR4, and it must PASS when SR1-SR4 already correctly discriminate. In practice this means SR5 should be implemented as a genuine end-to-end check that runs the naive/empty submission through SR1-SR4 grading logic and asserts they fail, exercised as part of the harness's own self-test at evaluator-construction time, not as a per-submission check that is invariant to submission content. (2) Add mutants/tests exercising FR3 (a submission where infected=true but suspect_nodes has fewer than 2 entries, and a submission where infected=false but suspect_nodes is non-empty) and FR4 (a submission where primary_output_affected does not match any port name in port_map.json, or is non-empty while infected=false). Ensure these mutants produce observable FR3/FR4 FAIL results so per_requirement_coverage shows FR3 and FR4 as covered:true before this case is considered fully verified.
